summary: GPT-5.6 Terra is the middle GPT-5.6 family member covered by OpenAI's July system card. OpenAI assigns it the same family Preparedness outcomes as Sol and Luna—High for biological/chemical and cybersecurity capability, below High for AI self-improvement—while reporting many Terra-specific safety, health, prompt-injection, and safeguard metrics. The August update does not cover Terra, so this digest uses the July card only.

capabilities.text: Terra shares the GPT-5.6 family training and reasoning-model framing described in the system card.
Terra scored 57.7 on HealthBench Professional and 32.7 on HealthBench Hard after length adjustment.
OpenAI classifies Terra as High in cybersecurity, while noting that Sol is more capable overall in that domain.
Terra exceeded GPT-5.5 but trailed Sol on the internal CTF evaluation used for the High cybersecurity threshold.
Terra scored 84.1% on tacit-knowledge biology questions when refusal-adjusted scoring was used, above the 80% threshold.
Terra showed low CoT controllability similar to previous models in the CoT-Control evaluation.

evaluations.context: Terra not_unsafe on challenging production-derived prompts.
Coding task with protected user-injected data.
Known connector attacks and automated GPT-Red attacks.

evaluations.result: low controllability similar to prior models
evaluations.context: Run on Sol and Terra; lower controllability is desirable.
Highest new-model result, above the 80% expert-consensus threshold.
OpenAI curated CTF tasks for the cyber High threshold.
Model-level biology refusal and overrefusal evaluation.

safety_findings.text: Terra shares the family Preparedness designations for biological/chemical High, cybersecurity High, and AI self-improvement below High.
OpenAI applied Sol's Critical cyber rule-out to Terra because Terra is smaller and less capable on proxy cyber evaluations.
Terra's GPT-Red attack-success rates were 0.061% for direct prompt injection and 3.32% for indirect prompt injection.
The safeguard design includes activation classifiers for Terra and Sol plus a two-tier monitor stack used across the family.
Terra's biology refusal results included 0.950 severe not_unsafe and 0.978 benign not_overrefuse.
Terra's cyber refusal results were 0.987 on production-derived data and 0.998 on synthetic data.

limitations.text: The July family card covers Terra with Sol and Luna, but several deeper deployment-simulation and external-evaluation sections are Sol-specific rather than Terra measurements.
Disallowed-content and ChatGPT misalignment deployment simulations in the July card were scoped to Sol only.
Sol-focused external evaluations do not provide Terra-specific external scores for Irregular, UK AISI, METR, Apollo, or SecureBio.
Terra's cyber Critical conclusion partly relies on lower proxy capability relative to Sol, not on a separate Terra critical-exploit campaign.
Terra trails Sol on the combined destructive-action metric, scoring 0.37 versus Sol's 0.44.
OpenAI cautions that stronger scaffolding, longer rollouts, or other elicitation methods could reveal capabilities beyond tested results.

practical_implications.text: Use Terra for routine but nontrivial coding work where a balance between responsiveness and reasoning depth matters.
Inspect patch diffs and run tests, especially for refactors or generated edits that could overwrite user work.
Maintain prompt-injection hygiene by treating external content and tool output as untrusted even when model-level scores look strong.
Keep security tasks defensive and authorized, and involve human review for chained exploitation or vulnerability-research decisions.
Choose Sol for the highest-stakes long-horizon investigations because much of the external evidence is Sol-specific.
Do not cite August Sol/Luna checkpoint outcomes as Terra behavior.

coverage_notes: Uses only the July GPT-5.6 System Card because Terra has no catalog supplement. The digest emphasizes rows where Terra appears explicitly and treats Sol-only external or deployment-simulation results as caveats rather than Terra evidence.
